data.name: Isharith
data.gender_notes: Isharith is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Isharith is a Sanskrit name derived from Isha, the female form of Shiva, the God of creation and destruction. Isharith signifies the lord or protector of Isha. In Hindu mythology, Isha is considered the embodiment of creative energy and power. The name Isharith carries the meaning “Lord of Isha” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Isharith usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of isha and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Isharith belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Isha.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Isharith total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Isharith represents the deep reverence and devotion towards Shiva, one of the most worshipped deities in Hinduism. The name carries the rich cultural heritage of India, where a personal name not only reflects one's personality and character, but also their faith and religious beliefs.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, Isharith is a name that embodies divine protection, power, and creativity. It signifies the belief in the all-powerful and all-providing nature of the universe, represented by Shiva. Wearing the name Isharith is a constant reminder of the divine presence and guidance, providing a sense of peace, strength, and purpose.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Isharith, meaning 'Rule of God', signifies the individual's complete surrender to the divine will. It is a reminder that true power lies in aligning oneself with the universal consciousness and allowing the divine to guide one's actions.

historical_references.reference: Ishvaran, a celebrated god in Shivaism, was known as Ishwara, the lord of all, whose name was Ishrita or Ishwara's consort. Ishwara, in turn, was identified with the supreme spirit Rudra.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology, Shivaism, Ishwara, Ishrita, Rudra

historical_references.reference: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, a seminal work in yoga philosophy, mention Ishvara as the supreme controller of the universe and the ultimate goal of yoga practice. In this context, Ishvara is often referred to as Paramatma, or the supreme self.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Isharith continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
